propositions: Commit bodies on main are inconsistently wrapped (5 of last 40 pass, 35 fail, with body lines ranging 72–286 characters), creating false impression of automatic reformatting.
Gerrit's bundled commit-message-length-validator only warns and is ignored; no local enforcement gate exists before commit.
A check-only script enforces subject ≤50 and body lines ≤72 at commit time, rejecting non-conforming commits and naming offending lines without mutating the message.
Gerrit's own commit-msg hook (which stamps Change-Id) must be preserved in migration mode (as commit-msg.legacy) to avoid breaking pushes when pre-commit installs the wrapping gate.
Specific carve-outs (trailers, TAG= lines, fenced blocks, indented literals, table rows, atomic tokens like URLs/paths) are exempt from the 72-column check per exact regex/threshold rules.
